AgentQuota.description:
The usage quota one agent program reports on a host, e.g. claude's `5h` and `week` windows.
Each machine is logged in to its own account, so the quota is per host. Sent when anything
but `read_at` changes, and once at host start.

exhausted.description: The program reports it is out of quota.

kind.description: The agent program, e.g. `claude`; a plain string, so a new program needs no schema change.

plan.description: The account's plan, when the program reports it, e.g. `plus`, `Pro`.

read_at.description: When the numbers were read at the source: their staleness, not the scan's.

AgentRenamed.description:
An agent's name was set by the fleet, not by herdr: the host restored the name herdr dropped
when the agent restarted in its pane. Written just before the
`agent.up` that carries the name; `rule` says which.

agent.description: The agent's full id after the rename.

from.description: The id it had until now (a pane-id name, `agent:<host>/<session>/<pane>`), when it had one.

rule.description: The rule that did it, e.g. `pane-name-memory`.

AgentRole.description:
An agent's declared level and the lead it reports to. Without `level` the agent's role is
removed.

domain.description: What a domain lead owns, e.g. `payments`.

AgentSignal.description:
A structured signal from the agent's own program — a harness hook (`agent-fleet hook
signal` / the statusline wrapper) writes it. `prompt` and `turn_end` open a new episode:
the fold drops the agent's stored signal on them. `detail` carries the program's own
text (an error message, a question) when there is one.

program.description: The agent program, e.g. `claude`; a plain string, so a new program needs no schema change.

AgentState.description: An agent's lifecycle state, as the terminal multiplexer reports it.

AgentStuck.description:
Why an agent on the writer's host is stopped, read off its screen. Sent when the cause
appears or changes; `cause` absent clears the record once the agent works again.

detail.description: What the screen showed, or what was done about it.

until.description: When the condition lifts: a quota window's reset, a rate-limit's retry.

AgentUnmanaged.description:
An agent program running outside every herdr pane tree on `host`, reported by the host's
process scan. `procs: 0`-style clearing: the next scan without it sends the same event minus
`program`.

program.description: The program (`claude`, `devin`, `codex`); absent clears the report.

since.description: When it was first seen unmanaged.

pane.description: Multiplexer pane currently hosting the agent.

AgentUsage.description: What an agent's processes cost: the pane's whole process tree, sampled by its host.

cpu_pct.description: CPU since the previous sample, in percent of one core.

rss_kb.description: Memory, CPU and process count are measured on Linux only; elsewhere just `cwd` is sent.

AskAnswered.description:
An operator's answer to the `ask.raised` named by `re`, given on the board. The answer reaches
the asker as the `msg.sent` named by `msg`, written in the same step.

answer.description: A chosen option or free text.

approve.description: An approval, not just an answer. Never implied by choosing an option.

approves.description: For an approval: the exact question text the approval applies to.

msg.description: The `msg.sent` that carries the answer to the asker.

context.description: A link to the context needed to answer.

owner.description: Who or what has to act: an agent, a resource, an ask.

pid.description:
A process on the raiser's host the block waits on (a lock holder). That host resolves
the blocker once the pid is gone or no longer started at `started`.

started.description: When `pid` started, read when the blocker was raised: a reused pid started later.

BlockerResolved.description: Resolves the `blocker.raised` named by the envelope's `re`.

DiskEntry.description: One large directory in a host's cached disk-use breakdown.

DiskReport.description:
The disk sample `disk_free`/`disk_total` came from. Free space is statvfs, never a traversal;
`breakdown` is the separate, cached `dust` answer to what uses the space.

behind_since.description:
Since when the host's fetch has found `origin/main` ahead of `commit`; absent when it is
not behind, or cannot tell.

commit.description: The commit the host's binary was built from; absent when built outside a git checkout.

disk.description: When the disk numbers were sampled, and the cached `dust` breakdown of what uses them.

disk_free.description: Bytes available to unprivileged users on the worktree volume, from the last disk sample.

machine.description:
The machine's load, core count and memory. Absent in reports from before host-load
heartbeats, or when the platform cannot read them.

repos.description:
Repositories this host serves (`[repos]` merged with its `--repo` flags), so routing can
tell whether another host can take a spawn.

HostStats.description:
The host agent's own vitals. Counters run from the host's start, so a drop in `uptime_s`
between two reports is a restart.

cpu_ms.description: User + system CPU time of the host process.

herdr_errors.description: Failed herdr calls and dropped herdr subscriptions.

max_rss_kb.description: Peak resident memory of the host process.

ring_failures.description: Rings that failed or were not followed by `working`.

spooled.description: Events this host sent to the spool instead of the hub.

write_failures.description: Events this host could neither send nor spool.

Level.description: An agent's declared level of responsibility, low to high.

MachineStats.description:
One machine's load and memory at a `host.health` report. Load is the system load average;
memory is bytes. `cores` is the online CPU count the load is compared against.

commit.description: The merge commit on the base branch, when `gh` reported it.

sha.description: The approved head that was merged.

MergeRequested.description:
`agent-fleet merge` for a repository whose fleet.toml `[merge] host` names another host asks
that host to run the whole merge: the verdict, pin and head checks, its gate, `gh pr merge`.

allow_pin_rewind.description: `--allow-pin-rewind`: the reason a submodule pin may move backwards.

sha.description: The approved head sha, or a prefix of it (7 to 40 hex digits).

MergeResult.description: The `merge.requested` named by `re`, answered by the host that ran it.

ok.description: False when nothing was merged: a refusal, a failed gate, an expired request, or an error.

text.description: What `agent-fleet merge` prints on that host: its last 4 KiB.

MsgDelivered.description: The `msg.sent` named by `re` reached the agent, which then turned `observed`.

ack.description:
The ring asked for an ack (`(ack: agent-fleet read)`): the tell stays unread, and is rung
again, until its recipient's `msg.read`. Absent on rings older than the ack.

attempts.description: Rings it took, this one included.

rung.description: When the ring that worked was typed.

MsgRead.description:
The recipient read the `msg.sent` named by `re` itself (`agent-fleet read`): its ack. Only
the agent the message reached counts; anyone else's `msg.read` is ignored.

MsgSent.description: A doorbell: a short prompt pointing at an event or a task.

closes.description:
A host's `DEADLETTER` digest: the tells it hands over, each taken off its recipient's
queue by this one event.

kind.description: What the recipient should do, e.g. `REVIEW`, `FYI`, `UNBLOCKED`.

ref.description: The event or task the message is about.

to.description:
A full agent id, or `coordinator`: whichever up agent holds the root-coordinator role
when the message is delivered.

PaneRefused.description:
`agent-fleet hook bash` refused `command` (the herdr argv it found, joined): it types into
`pane` on `host`, which `agent` holds.

ProcessHung.description:
A process an agent started that the watch tick found hung: at most 1% CPU, no change to a
stdout/stderr file, and no new or working child for two ticks in a row. `pid` is the
topmost hung process, `pids` it and every hung process under it. `evidence` absent clears
it (see `watch::to_clear`).

checked.description: When the host last confirmed it hung; it re-reports every tick it does.

evidence.description: CPU, the last output, the deepest descendant's command.

since.description: When it was first found hung.

ProcessOrphaned.description:
A process on the writer's host doctor proved an orphan: reparented to init with its
device gone, or a lock's recorded owner dead. `why`/`cwd`/`since` absent clears it —
the process is gone or somebody's parent chain claimed it.

cwd.description: Where it runs, when the platform reports one.

why.description: The proof: `"group leader dead"`, `"device gone"`, or `"<resource> lock owner dead"`.

QuotaWindow.description: One quota window: `used_pct` of the limit spent, resetting at `resets_at`.

ResourceHold.description:
A process holds (`resource.taken`) or queues for (`resource.waiting`) a resource on its host:
a lock the host reads.

resource.description: The host's name for it, e.g. `sim` or `build.1`.

scope.description: What the process says it is doing.

since.description: When it took the resource or joined the queue.

ResourceLimit.description:
A capacity rule: at most `max` worktrees hold any of `resources` on `host` at once, until
`until`. Replaces the rule of the same `name`; an empty `resources` removes it.

ResourceReleased.description: `pid` let go of the resource or left its queue. Without `pid`: nobody holds or waits for it.

RetireRequested.description:
`agent-fleet retire` run on a host that is not the agent's asks the agent's host to run the
retire itself: the pane, the locks and the repository's hook are all that host's.

decide.description: `delete`, `keep` or `stash`: what to do with real uncommitted changes.

host.description: The host that runs it: the agent's.

rule.description: The rule that asked, when a rule and not a person did: `idle.auto_retire`.

RetireResult.description: The `retire.requested` named by `re`, answered by the host that ran it.

ok.description: False when nothing was retired: refused over uncommitted changes, or an error.

text.description: What `agent-fleet retire` prints on that host.

SpawnRequested.description:
`agent-fleet spawn` (or `handoff`) asks the host agent on `host` to create a worktree (or a
workspace in an existing one), start the agent and give it the brief. The requester and the
host may be on different machines.

agent.description: The full id it will have: `agent:<host>/<session>/<name>`.

in_place.description:
Run in the host's own checkout of `repo`: no worktree, no branch, and retire only closes
the pane. Mutually exclusive with `worktree`.

lead.description: Whom the agent reports to; absent means the requester.

level.description: The `agent.role` level declared once the agent is up.

name.description: The agent's name in its session.

profile.description:
The routing profile that was picked. The host resolves its `kind`, `args`, `unset_env`
and the `ready` script from its checkout's `.agent-fleet/fleet.toml`, else the machine's
— a request never carries executable configuration.

replaces.description: An agent to close once the new one has taken its brief (a handoff).

repo.description: `owner/repo`; the host maps it to a checkout (`agent-fleet repo add`, `host --repo`).

session.description: The herdr session it runs in.

why.description: Every step of the routing decision, for the views.

worktree.description: An existing checkout: open a workspace there instead of creating a worktree.

SpawnResult.description: The `spawn.requested` named by `re`, answered by the host that ran it.

pane.description: The pane the agent runs in.

worktree.description: The worktree or checkout the agent works in.

StuckCause.description: Why an agent is stuck, as its host reads it off the screen.

oneOf.description: The program's account is out of quota.
A short rate-limit wait: `until` is when to retry.
A prompt sits in the input box, never sent.
The program's context is nearly full.
An error on screen waits on a nudge or a human.
A permission or trust prompt (herdr reports `blocked`, or the program signaled one).
The program is asking the operator something.
The program reports an account problem (billing, hold, auth).
Its worktree holds or waits on a resource; a legitimate wait, not a hang.
Its task is deliberately held: an open blocker or an unfinished dep.
Idle after working, nothing blocking on screen.
None of the above matched.

url.description: Where the spec lives (an issue, a doc).

TaskState.description: Task lifecycle, aligned with the A2A task states.

UpdateRequested.description:
`agent-fleet self-update` asks every host to pull its clone's `main`, rebuild and restart;
a host's own timer asks only itself, with `host`.

host.description: Only this host runs it. Absent: every host.

UpdateResult.description: One host's answer to the `update.requested` named by `re`.

commit.description:
The commit the host runs once restarted (the one it runs now when nothing changed); on
failure, the one it still runs.

WorktreeProcs.description:
Processes running in a worktree that no agent's process tree holds: dev servers, databases,
test runs, shells. Sent each scan while there are any, then once with `procs: 0`.

orphaned.description: The directory is gone: nothing that could stop these processes knows they are there.

WorktreeState.description: A git worktree on a host, as its last scan found it. Sent when it changes.

files.description: Files changed against the default branch, plus dirty ones; at most `MAX_FILES`.

herdr.description:
A linked worktree under herdr's worktree directory, where herdr and `agent-fleet spawn`
create them: only these can be `forgotten`.

in_main.description:
Everything this branch changed is already in the default branch (merged, squashed or
never started): it holds no work of its own.

repo.description: The main checkout the worktree belongs to.

unpushed.description: Commits on HEAD that no remote has.

event.description: Every event: the envelope fields plus a `type` tag and its `data`.

id.description: ULID chosen by the writer. Appending the same id twice is a no-op.

re.description: The event this one answers or follows.

v.description: Schema version of this event's type.

event.title: Event

finished.description:
When its state last became `done`; cleared on the next `working`. An agent that
finished its turn and sits idle is parked awaiting work, not stalled.

worked.description: When it was last seen `working`; a stall is an idle stretch after this.

AgentState.description: An agent's lifecycle state, as the terminal multiplexer reports it.

Answered.description: An ask the operator answered on the board, and how far the answer got.

acked.description: When the host saw the asker take the message; `None` while it is only sent.

approves.description: For an approval: the exact question text it applies to.

msg.description: The `msg.sent` that carries the answer to the asker.

pid.description: The process it waits on, on the raiser's host, and when that process started.

DiskEntry.description: One large directory in a host's cached disk-use breakdown.

DiskReport.description:
The disk sample `disk_free`/`disk_total` came from. Free space is statvfs, never a traversal;
`breakdown` is the separate, cached `dust` answer to what uses the space.

behind_since.description: Since when that commit has been behind `origin/main`, as its last `host.health` said.

commit.description: The commit its binary was built from, as its last `host.health` said.

disk.description: When the disk numbers were sampled, and the cached breakdown of what uses them.

machine.description: Machine load and memory from its last `host.health`; absent before host-load heartbeats.

repos.description: Repositories the host says it serves.

started.description: When the host process started: that report's time less its `uptime_s`.

Level.description: An agent's declared level of responsibility, low to high.

MachineStats.description:
One machine's load and memory at a `host.health` report. Load is the system load average;
memory is bytes. `cores` is the online CPU count the load is compared against.

Merge.description: A `merge.requested` and the `merge.result` that answered it.

MergeRequested.description:
`agent-fleet merge` for a repository whose fleet.toml `[merge] host` names another host asks
that host to run the whole merge: the verdict, pin and head checks, its gate, `gh pr merge`.

allow_pin_rewind.description: `--allow-pin-rewind`: the reason a submodule pin may move backwards.

sha.description: The approved head sha, or a prefix of it (7 to 40 hex digits).

MergeResult.description: The `merge.requested` named by `re`, answered by the host that ran it.

ok.description: False when nothing was merged: a refusal, a failed gate, an expired request, or an error.

text.description: What `agent-fleet merge` prints on that host: its last 4 KiB.

Orphan.description:
A process the host's scan proved an orphan: reparented to init, its device gone or its
lock's recorded owner dead.

ProcessHung.description:
A process an agent started that the watch tick found hung: at most 1% CPU, no change to a
stdout/stderr file, and no new or working child for two ticks in a row. `pid` is the
topmost hung process, `pids` it and every hung process under it. `evidence` absent clears
it (see `watch::to_clear`).

checked.description: When the host last confirmed it hung; it re-reports every tick it does.

evidence.description: CPU, the last output, the deepest descendant's command.

since.description: When it was first found hung.

Quota.description: A program's usage quota on one host, as its last `agent.quota` reported it.

exhausted_since.description:
When the reports first showed the account out; kept while it stays out, absent
while it does not.

read_at.description: When the numbers were read at the source: how stale they are.

ts.description: When the report was folded in.

QuotaWindow.description: One quota window: `used_pct` of the limit spent, resetting at `resets_at`.

by.description: The reader: the agent the message reached.

ResourceLimit.description:
A capacity rule: at most `max` worktrees hold any of `resources` on `host` at once, until
`until`. Replaces the rule of the same `name`; an empty `resources` removes it.

Retire.description: A `retire.requested` and the `retire.result` that answered it.

RetireRequested.description:
`agent-fleet retire` run on a host that is not the agent's asks the agent's host to run the
retire itself: the pane, the locks and the repository's hook are all that host's.

decide.description: `delete`, `keep` or `stash`: what to do with real uncommitted changes.

host.description: The host that runs it: the agent's.

rule.description: The rule that asked, when a rule and not a person did: `idle.auto_retire`.

RetireResult.description: The `retire.requested` named by `re`, answered by the host that ran it.

ok.description: False when nothing was retired: refused over uncommitted changes, or an error.

text.description: What `agent-fleet retire` prints on that host.

Role.description:
An agent's declared level and the lead it reports to; `by` and `since` record the
`agent.role` event that set it.

Spawn.description:
A `spawn.requested` and the `spawn.result` that answered it. `by` and `project` come from the
request's envelope.

answered.description: The answering event's `ts`; finished spawns are pruned 24 h after it.

SpawnRequested.description:
`agent-fleet spawn` (or `handoff`) asks the host agent on `host` to create a worktree (or a
workspace in an existing one), start the agent and give it the brief. The requester and the
host may be on different machines.

agent.description: The full id it will have: `agent:<host>/<session>/<name>`.

in_place.description:
Run in the host's own checkout of `repo`: no worktree, no branch, and retire only closes
the pane. Mutually exclusive with `worktree`.

lead.description: Whom the agent reports to; absent means the requester.

level.description: The `agent.role` level declared once the agent is up.

name.description: The agent's name in its session.

profile.description:

replaces.description: An agent to close once the new one has taken its brief (a handoff).

repo.description: `owner/repo`; the host maps it to a checkout (`agent-fleet repo add`, `host --repo`).

session.description: The herdr session it runs in.

why.description: Every step of the routing decision, for the views.

worktree.description: An existing checkout: open a workspace there instead of creating a worktree.

SpawnResult.description: The `spawn.requested` named by `re`, answered by the host that ran it.

pane.description: The pane the agent runs in.

worktree.description: The worktree or checkout the agent works in.

Stuck.description: An agent's current stuck record: the latest `agent.stuck` with a cause.

detail.description: What the screen showed, or what was done about it.

until.description: When the condition lifts, if the cause names one.

StuckCause.description: Why an agent is stuck, as its host reads it off the screen.

A short rate-limit wait: `until` is when to retry.
A prompt sits in the input box, never sent.
The program's context is nearly full.
An error on screen waits on a nudge or a human.
A permission or trust prompt (herdr reports `blocked`, or the program signaled one).
The program is asking the operator something.
The program reports an account problem (billing, hold, auth).
Its worktree holds or waits on a resource; a legitimate wait, not a hang.

TaskState.description: Task lifecycle, aligned with the A2A task states.

Unmanaged.description: An agent program the host's scan saw outside every herdr pane tree.

Unread.description: A delivered doorbell not read yet.

delivered.description: The last delivery's `ts`: the retransmit clock starts here.

rings.description: Deliveries so far, the first one included.

host.description: The one host it asks, or every host.

results.description: Each host's answer, by host name.

since.description:
The request's `ts`; the update is pruned `UPDATE_KEPT` after it, unless a host still runs
the commit its failed answer reports.

UpdateResult.description: One host's answer to the `update.requested` named by `re`.

commit.description:
The commit the host runs once restarted (the one it runs now when nothing changed); on
failure, the one it still runs.

Waiting.description: An agent's last `BLOCKED` or `QUESTION`, open until the lead tells it anything or it works.

rung.description: The host already re-rang the lead (`STILL-WAITING`).

WorktreeProcs.description:
Processes running in a worktree that no agent's process tree holds: dev servers, databases,
test runs, shells. Sent each scan while there are any, then once with `procs: 0`.

orphaned.description: The directory is gone: nothing that could stop these processes knows they are there.

WorktreeState.description: A git worktree on a host, as its last scan found it. Sent when it changes.

files.description: Files changed against the default branch, plus dirty ones; at most `MAX_FILES`.

herdr.description:
A linked worktree under herdr's worktree directory, where herdr and `agent-fleet spawn`
create them: only these can be `forgotten`.

in_main.description:
Everything this branch changed is already in the default branch (merged, squashed or
never started): it holds no work of its own.

repo.description: The main checkout the worktree belongs to.

unpushed.description: Commits on HEAD that no remote has.

answers.description: Asks answered on the board, by the id of their `ask.raised`; kept for 24 h after the ack.

asks.description: Open asks by the id of their `ask.raised`.

blockers.description: Open blockers by the id of their `blocker.raised`.

escalated.description: Tells handed back to their sender as `UNREAD` (`escalations`), kept while they are queued.

first_cwd.description:
The cwd an agent's own host first reported for its pane (`agent.usage`), by agent id; fixed
until `agent.down`, so a later `cd` does not move it. The root of an agent nobody spawned.

gone.description:
When each agent that is not up went down (`agent.down`), kept 24 h: a tell to it goes to
the coordinator `GONE_AFTER` later, never on a listing flap.

held_streak.description:
The last `HELD` text rung per agent and how many times in a row: the host backs off an
unchanged one. Gone once the agent works, changes state, goes down or is rung `IDLE`.

hung.description: Hung processes by `<host>:<pid>` of the topmost one, `since` always set.

idle_rung.description:
When the host last rang an agent's lead `IDLE`/`HELD` (key: the agent id) or `UNMANAGED`
(key: the id + `UNMANAGED_KEY`); gone once the agent works or goes down.

last.description: Id of the last event folded in.

lead_idled.description:
Agents the host has rung `IDLE` since they came up. A domain-lead is asked once: this
outlives a state change, unlike `idle_rung`. Gone on `agent.down`.

left_pane.description:
When each agent last left its pane without the pane closing (`agent.down` "agent left the
pane"): it is about to come back, so its spawn record outlives the usual 24 h meanwhile.

merges.description: Merge requests by their `merge.requested` id, kept for 24 h.

msgs.description: Undelivered doorbells by the id of their `msg.sent`.

orphans.description: Processes each host proved orphaned, keyed `<host>:<pid>`.

quotas.description: Usage quotas of the agent programs by `<host>:<kind>`.

read.description: Read doorbells by the id of their `msg.sent`, kept for 24 h after the read.

refused_kills.description: The latest kills `agent-fleet kill` refused, oldest first; at most `MAX_REFUSED`.

refused_panes.description:
The latest herdr writes into another agent's pane `hook bash` refused, oldest first; at
most `MAX_REFUSED`.

reports.description: Each up agent's last `msg.sent`, what `IDLE` quotes and `auto_retire` reads (`DONE`/`MERGED`).

retires.description: Retire requests by their `retire.requested` id, kept for 24 h.

roles.description: Declared roles by agent id; kept apart from `agents`, so a role survives `agent.down`.

signals.description:
The latest `agent.signal` per agent, keyed by agent id; cleared when a `prompt` or
`turn_end` signal opens a new episode, and when the agent turns `working` or goes down.

spawns.description: Spawn requests by their `spawn.requested` id; answered ones are kept for 24 h.

stuck.description: Why a stopped agent is stopped, as its host read it off the screen, keyed by agent id.

told.description:
When each agent's lead last told it anything: new work after a `DONE`, so `auto_retire`
waits for a fresh one. Gone when the agent goes down.

unknown.description:
Events this binary cannot fold (an unknown type, or a known type at a newer `v`): kept in
the log, skipped here.

unmanaged.description: Agent programs outside herdr on each host, keyed `<host>:<pid>`.

unread.description: Delivered doorbells their recipient has not read (`msg.read`) yet: retransmitted until it does.

updates.description: Self-update requests by their `update.requested` id, kept for 24 h.

waiting.description: Each agent's open `BLOCKED`/`QUESTION` to its lead, until answered (see `Waiting`).

worktree_procs.description: Processes running in worktrees (or orphaned beside them) by `<host>:<path>`.
